items.title: terraria
items.summaryPlot: long ago, the ancient race of dryads went to war with the cosmic entity cthulhu, tearing off some of his limbs before he retreated to the dark side of the moon. centuries later, you, the terrarian, venture into the world to stop cthulhu—now known as the moon lord—for good.
pros: unlike aimless survival sandboxes that rely entirely on self-directed goals, progression here is defined by clear milestones.
accessories, set bonuses and weapon mechanics demand distinct build optimization (melee, ranged, magic, summoner) that rewards strategic arena construction and synergy mastery over brute force.

unlike modern accessible sandboxes, it functions with overlapping systems (gear progression, biome management, boss summoning sequences, event mechanics) that reward planning and optimization over passive exploration.
boss fights demand strategies, arena construction and strict bullet hell patterns.
invasions, blood moons and solar eclipses break up the standard gameplay loop with sudden waves that test base defenses and player gear.
the late-game mobility options (grappling hooks, wings, dashes, boots), variety is unmatched.
unique biome mechanics (such as jungle poison hazards, desert sandstorms and underworld lava) force players to adapt their gear and strategies per region.
from hardly jumping 2 blocks to gain abilities of double jump, grappling hooks and even flying with wings, specially abilities and accessories deepens the core gameplay seriously.
sandbox of the game gives the co-op experience the creativity of designing custome sports using american football ball, golf or complex electric mechanism.
cons: game has high reliance at guides and wikis, reliance on external factors is serious negative.
certain essential crafting materials and accessories rely on low percentage chance drops, introducing frustrating artificial padding rather than skill-based acquisition.
the expansion of corruption/crimson and hallow ruins structural builds and npc housing unless countered with expensive cleansing grinds which is also waste of serious time.
the core pacing is broken, grinding for multi dozen of hours just to fight a boss to advance is artificial length expansion.
while the town/npc system provides vendors, the requirements (a box with a door, light and chair) and happiness mechanics feel surface-level.
preparing for high-tier boss encounters requires repetitive terraforming and placing platforms/buff stations across large segments of the map.

the game gifts you strongest weapons of the game after defeating moon lord which is the last boss, gamer never gets a chance to try them on well-designed boss-fights, the only usage is left as power fantasy by restarting the game which is dull.
certain classes (like summoner) suffer from awkward progression gaps and weak survivability at specific stages of the game compared to more straightforward builds.

items.title: call of duty: black ops ii
items.summaryPlot: the campaign follows two interconnected timelines: in the 1980s, alex mason and frank woods pursue the rise of the nicaraguan arms dealer raul menendez, while in 2025, mason's son david must stop menendez from sparking a second cold war by hacking the us drone fleet. the narrative is shaped by player choices and features multiple endings.
pros: unlike traditional arcade/corridor shooters, black ops ii introduces genuine cause-and-effect narrative branches.
it rejects the typical bulletproof hero fantasy in favor of messy, vulnerable characters.
menendez's terror network (cordis die) stems directly from anti-imperialist rage and personal tragedy.
the sound design (drones, emps, kinetic railguns) and environmental audio create a tactile soundscape.
the game avoids cheap plot armors or magical hand-waving, enforcing permanent consequences for mechanical/decision failures.
the narrative cleanly bridges historical proxy conflicts with near-future cyber warfare.
cons: the tactical strike force missions which mix squad management with fps controls are severely undercut by unresponsive allied ai.
the game frequently wrests control away from the player for cinematic qtes, jet piloting or scripted explosions that prioritize cinematic aura over mechanical depth.
jumping rapidly through gimmick encounters such as horseback rocket launching, drone piloting and rts command menus causes disruption to smooth gameplay rhythm.
while menendez has strong motives, much of the military dialogue relies on generic gruff soldier tropes and predictable hollywood action cliché.
sci-fi environment is not designed well.
some pivotal narrative forks rely on obscure actions (shooting a character in the leg vs. head without clear ui prompts) that feel like trial-and-error checks rather than strategic choices.
outside of scripted interactables, the environment is mostly static glass and concrete. lacking the deep sandbox physics or systems present in immersive titles.

items.title: neon genesis evangelion
items.summaryPlot: in 2015, fifteen years after a cataclysm known as the second impact, the teenage shinji ikari is summoned to tokyo-3 by his estranged father gendo to pilot the giant biomechanical weapon evangelion unit-01 against monstrous beings called angels, who threaten humanity's existence. as shinji and his fellow pilots rei ayanami and asuka langley soryu battle these entities, they are forced to confront their own deep psychological traumas while uncovering the terrifying truth about nerv, the evas, and their father's secret human instrumentality project—a plan to forcibly merge all human souls into a single, unified consciousness.
pros: unlike traditional mecha anime that glorify young pilots as heroic power fantasies, evangelion presents piloting as a brutal and traumatic ordeal.
the evas are organic and bleeding cybernetic monsters with later-on, adds a lot to the emotional weight.
the magic/combat system relies on hard-boundary mechanics, is very disciplined and contains zero aura-farming scenes. fights are resolved through physics, engineering and environmental mechanics.
the series constructs a claustrophobic world burdened by post-cataclysmic doom and inescapable psychological isolation.

characters are dissected through psychoanalytic frameworks (hedgehog's dilemma, freudian/jungian trauma). their coping mechanisms and flaws are treated as realistic psychological systems rather than melodramatic cartoon tropes.
every adult figure has broken motives, this causes an anti-authoritarian aspect and is well-used in the show.

as gainax ran out of time and budget near the end, hideaki anno leaned into unpolished experimental methods such as still frames, text-on-screen and claustrophobic interior monologues. this is well-made with artistic intent.
political ecosystems and characters are overally well-written.
trauma and over-melodrama is deserved, psychological foundations are well-built and functional.
cons: episodes 7 through 13 shift into a relatively monster-of-the-week procedural loop.
early to mid-series episodes rely on anime comedy tropes such as accidental nudity, slapstick reactions and harem dynamics between shinji, asuka and misato.
the original tv finale abandons the physical plot resolution, leaving the fate of the real world, nerv and the angels unresolved on screen in favor of abstract psychoanalytical slide shows.
the christian/kabbalah imagery (crosses, angels, dead sea scrolls) is largely deployed for aesthetic atmosphere and surface flavor rather than a fully mapped theology system. systematic fillers.
classmates like toji, kensuke,and hikari are given promising setups but are eventually dropped or marginalized.
shadowy figures whispering vague, cryptic exposition in dark rooms, relying on over-explained mystery, basically are just dumps.
mediumInfluences: nausicaä of the valley of the wind

items.title: mezzanine
items.summaryPlot: constructing an cinematic soundscape of dread. it evokes a world of shadows and paranoia, exploring themes of disillusion, depression and decay through dark, intense, and often foreboding sonic textures.
pros: mezzanine rejects the thin and bright production of mainstream 90s pop in favor of a heavy and oppressive frequency space.
album injects harsh and distorted post-punk guitars (angelo bruschini) into dark electronic beats.
the vocal contributions from horace andy’s fragile but haunting falsetto to elizabeth fraser's ethereal but non-verbal phrasing on "teardrop" are free of ego and rejects performative approach.
uncanny nocturnal atmosphere that mirrors the cold existential weight.
layered elemental richness without formualic pop cheapness.
drumming in the album anchors the chaotic guitar swells and synth drones, maintaining a grounded center.
the album excels at patient slow-burn arrangements that erupt into intense loud breakdowns.
album contains zero thematic fillers.
cons: across the 63-minute, the album relies exclusively on mid-to-slow tempo drag. the lack of sharp rhythmic speed variance across the middle tracks causes the pacing to feel stagnant.
the lyrics across the album are obscured, abstract or intentionally fragmented.
some tracks relies on constant sample-loops and these segments are insanely long, this situation causes fatique quickly.
the track "teardrop" contains many cliché mainstream pop elements unlike the overall approach of the album.
certain tracks feel like isolated studio experiments stitched together rather than a seamlessly written band unit.
